raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #50046. When `compile_sizes` is set, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` with TP=4 dies at start-up, during CUDA-graph memory profiling, with `AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 4097==512 at dim=0`. The cause is `create_concrete_args` in `vllm/compilation/piecewise_backend.py`. It set every symbol, stride symbols included, to the compile size. With this fix, a symbol that Dynamo created only for an input's stride or storage offset keeps its traced value.

Compared with #50445, this fix:

- Also fixes the stride where the graph takes the stride symbol as a SymInt input. [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) still sets that symbol to the compile size, so on Qwen3.5 every single-size graph passes `positions_stride_m` = size to the fused M-RoPE kernel, and the crash becomes silently wrong H/W positions. With vLLM's `fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate` at compile size 16, [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) gives output that differs from eager (`Tensor-likes are not close!`), and this fix matches eager.
- Does not break a case that works today. Take a tensor with no token dim whose stride is the token count, passed across a split: with [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) the size-16 graph fails with `stride 16==64`, and the old code and this fix both pass.
- Adds a test that catches the bug. [#50445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50445) adds no test.

## Claims

- The command from the issue now starts and serves requests on 4 x H200 with torch 2.14, instead of failing in CUDA-graph memory profiling.
- Graphs compiled for a single entry of `compile_sizes` now keep input strides and storage offsets that do not depend on the token count. Here that is the M-RoPE positions row pitch, 4097. Sizes, SymInt inputs and unbacked sizes still become the compile size, as before.
- New test `test_compile_sizes_keep_input_strides` in `tests/compile/test_compile_ranges.py`. That file already runs in CI.

## Validation

Hardware and software: 4 x NVIDIA H200, torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7` (commit `49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`), and this commit on top of it for the "after" runs.

Reproducer: the command from the issue. No request is needed, because the bug stops the server at start-up. I added `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` because it was needed to get past NCCL start-up on the test machine. It is not related to the bug.

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 \
VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config.compile_sizes '[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512]' \
  --compilation-config.cudagraph_capture_sizes '[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512]'
```

Before (base commit, 1 run from a source install, failed 1 of 1; the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image of the same commit also failed 3 of 3):

```
assert_size_stride_grouped((arg13_1, arg14_1, arg15_1, arg16_1), ((256, ), (256, ), (262144, 64), (3, 512)), ((1, ), (1, ), (64, 1), (512, 1)), 'input')
AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 4097==512 at dim=0
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After (patched tree, 2 runs: one by me and one by a separate check). Both runs compiled every graph from scratch, and both passed:

```
[backbone] Compiling a graph for compile range (512, 512) takes 118.04 s
Graph capturing finished in 7 secs, took 0.48 GiB
Available KV cache memory: 30.08 GiB
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Neither log has an `AssertionError` or a `Traceback`. In both runs, two chat requests at temperature 0 got correct answers ("Paris", and a count from 1 to 30 in 110 tokens). In the second run, 16 copies of the counting request sent at the same time all gave the same correct answer. Both servers exited with code 0 on SIGTERM.

If you rerun this: the AOT compile cache key does not include `vllm/compilation/*.py`. An entry built by the old code on the same GPU model is loaded as-is, and then the fix never runs. Clear `~/.cache/vllm/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/` first.

Unit test: `python -m pytest -W error::FutureWarning tests/compile/test_compile_ranges.py -v`. With the fix, 5 passed. With the old `piecewise_backend.py`, the new test fails with `AssertionError: expected size 3==3, stride 8193==16 at dim=0`, and the 4 existing tests pass.

Older torch: I ran `create_concrete_args` alone on Dynamo graphs with CPU torch 2.10.0 and 2.11.0, and with torch 2.14.0, under `-W error::FutureWarning`. Plain, fixed-offset and strided inputs all give the expected shape, stride and offset on all three versions. For example, the strided input gives `((3, 16), (8193, 1), 0)`.

`pre-commit` passes on both changed files. I did not run an accuracy eval (`lm_eval`).

## Details

Root cause: `create_concrete_args` came in with #35472. It builds the example inputs for graphs compiled for one entry of `compile_sizes`, and it replaced every free symbol in each input's shape, stride and storage offset with the compile size. The M-RoPE `positions` input is `RopeState.positions[:, :num_tokens]`, a slice of a persistent `(3, max_num_tokens + 1)` = `(3, 4097)` buffer. Dynamo gives its row stride a symbol of its own, with traced value 4097. The old code set that symbol to 512, so the size-512 graph asserted stride `(512, 1)`, but the real tensor has stride `(4097, 1)`. Inductor size asserts are on by default for torch >= 2.12, so the assert fails during CUDA-graph capture. On torch < 2.12 the asserts are off by default. There the old code did not crash, but the kernels in the size graphs would read M-RoPE rows 1 and 2 at the wrong offset. This change fixes that case too. I did not run the model on torch < 2.12.

Fix: a symbol is a layout symbol when all of its Dynamo sources (`shape_env.var_to_sources`) are `TensorPropertySource` with a property other than `SIZE`. A layout symbol keeps its traced value, from `shape_env.backed_var_to_val` on torch >= 2.11 or from `var_to_val` before that. Every other symbol takes exactly the old path. I added a temporary debug print and ran the real model with it. The only symbol the fix changes there is `positions.stride(0)`: the old value was the compile size (1 to 512), and the new value is 4097, for every size on all 4 ranks.

Why ask Dynamo where the symbol came from, instead of the simpler options:

- Giving every stride its traced value is wrong for contiguous inputs, whose stride does depend on the size.
- Calling a symbol a size only when it appears in a shape gets it wrong for a size symbol that appears only in a stride, or only as a SymInt input of a subgraph.

Tradeoff: a size graph now fixes each layout symbol to its traced value, not to the compile size. Take a caller that traces with a strided view and later passes a contiguous tensor at a compile size. That worked by chance before, and it now fails the size assert. No vLLM runner does this: MRV1, MRV2 and the spec-decode proposer pass a slice of the same persistent buffer at trace time and at run time.

Not fixed here: one combination fails in the range graph, on the old code and the new code alike. It is unbacked dynamic shapes, plus M-RoPE positions, plus a splitting op. The error is `AssertionError: Shape: 8193 out of considered ranges: [(1, 8192)]`. The cause is that `PiecewiseBackend.__call__` dispatches on the first SymInt input, and there that input is the stride symbol. It needs a different change.

---

files.patch:
@@ -209,6 +209,52 @@ def test_compile_sizes_produce_static_shapes(disable_vllm_compile_cache):
     )
 
 
+def scale_by_positions(x: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return x * (positions[0] + 2 * positions[1] + 3 * positions[2]).unsqueeze(-1)
+
+
+@support_torch_compile(dynamic_arg_dims={"x": 0, "positions": -1})
+class MRoPEPositionsModel(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = "", **kwargs) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return scale_by_positions(x, positions)
+
+
+def test_compile_sizes_keep_input_strides(disable_vllm_compile_cache):
+    """A compile_sizes graph must keep input strides that do not depend on
+    the size, like M-RoPE positions sliced from a persistent
+    (3, max_num_tokens + 1) buffer (issue #50046)."""
+    max_num_tokens = 8192
+    torch.set_default_device("cuda")
+    vllm_config = VllmConfig(
+        scheduler_config=SchedulerConfig(
+            max_num_batched_tokens=max_num_tokens,
+            max_model_len=max_num_tokens,
+            is_encoder_decoder=False,
+        ),
+        compilation_config=CompilationConfig(
+            mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE,
+            compile_sizes=[16],
+        ),
+    )
+    positions_buffer = torch.randint(0, 100, (3, max_num_tokens + 1))
+
+    with (
+        set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+        torch.inference_mode(),
+        set_forward_context({}, vllm_config=vllm_config),
+    ):
+        model = MRoPEPositionsModel(vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix="").eval()
+        for num_tokens in [BATCH_SIZE, 16]:
+            x = torch.randn(num_tokens, MLP_SIZE)
+            positions = positions_buffer[:, :num_tokens]
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                model(x, positions), scale_by_positions(x, positions)
+            )
+
+
 def test_inductor_cache_compile_ranges(disable_vllm_compile_cache):
     # disable_vllm_compile_cache sets VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 to force
     # multiple compilations by disabling vLLM's on-disk compile cache.

@@ -19,6 +19,7 @@
 from vllm.config import VllmConfig
 from vllm.config.utils import Range
 from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import is_torch_equal_or_newer
 
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
@@ -39,17 +40,42 @@ def create_concrete_args(graph: fx.GraphModule, size: int) -> list[Any]:
 
     Used for single-size compilation where we need concrete-shaped inputs.
     The Dynamo-captured graph gives us example inputs with SymInts in them.
+    Symbols that Dynamo created only for an input's stride or storage offset
+    keep their traced value. They are assumed not to change with the size
+    (e.g. the row pitch of a slice of a persistent buffer).
     """
+    from torch._dynamo.source import TensorProperty, TensorPropertySource
     from torch._prims_common import compute_required_storage_length
     from torch._subclasses.fake_tensor import FakeTensorMode
     from torch.fx.experimental.symbolic_shapes import ShapeEnv, is_symbolic
 
+    def is_layout_symbol(shape_env: ShapeEnv, s: Any) -> bool:
+        sources = shape_env.var_to_sources.get(s)
+        return bool(sources) and all(
+            isinstance(src, TensorPropertySource)
+            and src.prop is not TensorProperty.SIZE
+            for src in sources
+        )
+
     def concretize(sym_val: Any) -> int:
-        """Replace all symbolic variables in a SymInt expression with size."""
+        """Replace size symbols with size, layout symbols with traced values."""
         if not is_symbolic(sym_val):
             return int(sym_val)
+        shape_env = sym_val.node.shape_env
+        traced_vals = (
+            shape_env.backed_var_to_val
+            if is_torch_equal_or_newer("2.11.0")
+            else shape_env.var_to_val
+        )
         expr = sym_val.node.expr
-        return int(expr.subs({s: size for s in expr.free_symbols}))
+        return int(
+            expr.subs(
+                {
+                    s: traced_vals[s] if is_layout_symbol(shape_env, s) else size
+                    for s in expr.free_symbols
+                }
+            )
+        )
 
     fake_mode = FakeTensorMode(shape_env=ShapeEnv())
